previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with acute left neck pain that began after cracking his neck, later associated with fevers and neurological symptoms. Initial imaging ruled out dissection, but blood cultures revealed Streptococcus bovis bacteremia. MRI showed findings concerning for osteomyelitis and septic arthritis of the left claviculomanubrial joint. Due to a penicillin allergy, he underwent successful ceftriaxone desensitization in the MICU and was started on a six-week course of IV antibiotics via PICC line. A colonoscopy identified and removed five colonic adenomas, likely the source of bacteremia. Warfarin was discontinued as his prior pulmonary embolism was provoked and adequately treated. His pain resolved with multimodal management, and he was discharged home with nursing support, stable vital signs, and clear mental status.
problems: Septic arthritis of the sternoclavicular joint

and recent travel history, the differential on admission was

tenderness over his frontal and maxillary sinuses, and this was 
also demonstrated in his CT head. In addition his ESR at 72

signs that would be concerning for vascular causes of headache, 
the headache was not of sudden onset, and he did not have any 
cranial nerve findings that would go along with this.   On 
examination.  Given history of multiple myeloma and distant 
history of prostate and testicular cancer, concern for 
leptomeningeal disease and occasionally, the CSF may not be 
impressive in the beginning stages. An MRI of his head and 
orbits revealed no evidence of metastatic disease.   Mr. ___ 
headache resolved by HD 3 and he was discharged to home with 
resolution of maxillary and frontal sinus tenderness and ear 
pain.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with headache and right eye pain.

COMPARISON:  CT of the head from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were acquired through the head without contrast. 
Multiplanar reformations were obtained and reviewed.

FINDINGS:

No acute hemorrhage, large vascular territory infarct, shift of midline
structures or mass effect is present.  There is an old lacunar infarct in the
left basal ganglia (2:11).  The visible paranasal sinuses and mastoid air
cells are well aerated. Mild fat stranding noted in the soft tissues at the
left convexity (image 30, series 2), likely scar and granulation tissue.

IMPRESSION:

No acute intracranial process.

HISTORY:  ___ male with history of PE and multiple myeloma.  Patient
now presents with headache and subjective fevers.  Evaluation for possible
dural venous thrombosis.

COMPARISON:  Non-contrast head CT from ___ at 4:59 a.m.

TECHNIQUE:  After injection of 90 cc of IV contrast material, delayed axial
imaging was performed from the skull base through the brain.  Sagittal and
coronal reformations were done.  Images were processed on a separate
workstation with display of volume-rendered images and maximum intensity
projection images.

CT VENOGRAM:

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of dural venous thrombosis or occlusion.  No
definitive arterial thrombosis or occlusion is identified on these delayed
venous phase images.  There is no evidence of aneurysm formation or other
vascular abnormality on the axial images.

Compared to the prior non-contrast CT, again visualized is mild symmetrical
prominence of the ventricles and sulci consistent with cortical atrophy.  A
previously seen left basal ganglia lacunar infarct appears unchanged.  No
intra- or extra-axial hemorrhage, edema, masses, or acute large territory
infarction is identified.  Again seen is mild fat stranding in the soft
tissues of the left convexity likely related to scar formation or granulation
tissue.  There is diffuse mucosal thickening of the left maxillary sinus and
the bilateral sphenoid sinuses.  On the current examination, there appears to
be opacification of the left mastoid air cells, which was not clearly
visualized on the prior CT.  No other significant change compared to the prior
exam.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of dural venous thrombosis or occlusion.
2.  No definitive arterial thrombosis or vascular malformation on this venous
phase study.
3.  Opacification of the left mastoid air cells, which was not clearly
visualized on the prior non-contrast head CT.
4.  No other significant change compared to the prior examination.

MRI BRAIN AND ORBIT.

COMPARISON:  CTA head ___.

HISTORY:  Multiple myeloma, hypertension, diabetes, prostate and testicular
cancer status post treatment, presents with headaches and proptosis, evaluate
for metastatic disease to the orbital area.

TECHNIQUE:  Whole-brain multiplanar T2, FLAIR, diffusion-weighted, and
post-contrast imaging was performed.  Axial and coronal T1 imaging and coronal
STIR and post-contrast imaging through the orbits was also obtained with fat
saturation.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of acute infarction or abnormal enhancement. 
There is no shift of normally midline structures.  The ventricles and sulci
are normal in appearance.  There is normal gray-white matter differentiation. 
The orbits are unremarkable.  There is no definite evidence of proptosis or
abnormal enhancement within the orbits.  The optic nerves are intact
bilaterally.  The extraocular muscles are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of metastatic disease within the brain and
specifically within the orbits.  Scattered T2 and FLAIR abnormality within the
periventricular and subcortical white matter likely represents sequelae of
chronic microvascular ischemic changes.
